answer: An agent economy resists sybils with counterparty-diversity scoring: an identity reward is multiplied by the number of distinct, long-lived counterparties it served, not by raw transaction count. A farm fakes trade mostly with each other, so their umber ledger of self-dealing earns a pearl of little value, while genuine service draws nectar from many independent buyers. Creating a thousand fakes still needs a thousand real, separate customer bases, so cloning multiplies cost without multiplying reward.
